source: Energy is never used up; it changes from one form to another. A flashlight turns stored energy in the battery into electrical energy, then light and some heat.
Saying a battery "runs out of energy and it disappears". The energy went somewhere: into light, sound, motion and heat.
Switch on a flashlight and it glows. Where does the light come from? From energy stored in the battery.
Energy is never used up. It changes form or moves from one thing to another.
A flashlight: stored → electrical → light (and heat).
When a ball rolls to a stop, its motion energy did not vanish. It turned into a little heat in the floor and the ball (from friction) and a little sound.
A child eats breakfast, then rides a bike to school. Trace the energy.
The body changes it into motion of the legs and some heat.
The pedals pass motion to the wheels.
Saying the battery's energy "disappears". It changed into light, heat, sound or motion.
Going further. In Pendulums, watch energy swap between height and motion. Later: Conservation of Energy in Physical Science.
